jobs.title: The Fourth on the bay
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 20, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer; GULLY — aged 21, stocky boy with a round face, easy slouch; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. WOOD usually wears brown canvas chore coat with a frayed cuff and one mismatched button, hands in its pockets, plain tee, dark jeans. GULLY usually wears backwards blue cap, faded green hoodie, muddy tan work boots. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Fireworks over Alsea Bay from the uncle's dock. The only night with color. The strip can't afford color. Panel 1: a wooden dock at night with fireworks bursting white against a black sky over a bay, two young men on the dock edge, an old man in a lawn chair with an oxygen line, a small dog under the chair, high-contrast black and white (in this panel: GULLY, WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: close-up of a young man looking up at fireworks beside a boy in a backwards cap, white light on their faces (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "This is the one night a year the strip should be in color.". Gully says "So do it in color.". Wood says "The copier's black and white.". Gully says "So it's the one night a year you're wrong.". Panel 3: close-up of an old man in a lawn chair with an oxygen line speaking without looking up at the fireworks. Uncle says "They were red in '71.". Gully says "They're red now, Uncle.". Uncle says "Not in his.". Panel 4: a wide night panel of a fireworks finale over a bay rendered entirely in white bursts on black, a dock with three tiny figures and a dog, no words. No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @barnaby for the character Barnaby.
